cor.heading: Cost of Goods Sold
cor.text: Cost of goods sold was $2,887 million and $8,888 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $2,995 million and $8,756 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. As a percentage of net sales, cost of goods sold was 78.4% and 80.8%, respectively, compared with 80.9% and 80.4% in the prior-year periods. The quarter benefited from $109 million of tariff refunds recognized during the period, partially offset by lower production volumes. Year-to-date, lower production volumes more than offset the benefit of $114 million of tariff refunds, resulting in a modest increase in cost of goods sold as a percentage of net sales.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses
rd.text: Research and development expenses ("R&D") were $223 million and $685 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $281 million and $683 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The third quarter of 2025 included a $49 million impairment charge related to IPR&D assets from the 2023 Bennamann acquisition. Excluding this charge, year-to-date expenses were modestly higher than the prior-year period, reflecting continued investment in product development initiatives.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A") were $490 million and $1,449 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $549 million and $1,413 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. As a percentage of total revenues, SG&A was 11.3% and 11.2%, respectively, compared with 12.5% and 10.9% in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the three-month period primarily reflects lower risk costs in the Financial Services segment and the benefit of cost reduction actions. The increase in the nine-month period was primarily driven by increased labor costs.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A") were $490 million and $1,449 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $549 million and $1,413 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. As a percentage of total revenues, SG&A was 11.3% and 11.2%, respectively, compared with 12.5% and 10.9% in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the three-month period primarily reflects lower risk costs in the Financial Services segment and the benefit of cost reduction actions. The increase in the nine-month period was primarily driven by increased labor costs.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense was $358 million and $1,095 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared with $378 million and $1,100 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decreases were primarily driven by lower average debt balances, partially offset by higher interest rates.

Interest expense attributable to Industrial Activities, net of interest income and eliminations, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $30 million and $94 million, respectively, compared with $26 million and $77 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net interest expense was primarily driven by lower average cash balances available for investment, resulting in reduced interest income.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Income tax expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $204 million and $251 million, respectively, compared with $1 million and $124 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rates for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were 89.9% and 60.9%, respectively, compared with 2.0% and 25.4% in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

The increase in income tax expense and effective tax rates was primarily driven by a $156 million non-cash valuation allowance charge recorded in the third quarter of 2026 against DTAs in CNH’s Financial Services segment in Brazil. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had incurred cumulative losses in Brazil over the preceding 36 months, which represented significant objective negative evidence regarding the realizability of these DTAs and limited management’s ability to place significant reliance on projections of future taxable income. Management's assessment of the realizability of DTAs requires significant judgment regarding the timing and amount of future taxable income and is subject to assumptions and uncertainties related to future operating results, economic and market conditions in Brazil, future delinquencies, and interest rate movements.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Financial Services recorded a net loss of $77 million and net income of $68 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, a decrease of $124 million and $156 million compared with the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decreases in both periods were primarily driven by a $156 million non-cash valuation allowance charge against DTAs in Brazil recorded during the third quarter of 2026, unfavorable currency translation impacts, and lower volumes in South America and North America, partially offset by lower risk costs in South America. Year-to-date results were also impacted by higher SG&A expenses, specifically labor costs.

In the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, retail loan originations, including unconsolidated joint ventures, were $2.5 billion and $7.2 billion, respectively, a decrease of $0.2 billion and $0.6 billion compared with the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. The managed portfolio, including unconsolidated joint ventures, was $27.8 billion as of September 30, 2026 (comprised of 70% retail and 30% wholesale), a decrease of $0.7 billion compared with September 30, 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, receivables greater than 30 days past due represented 4.1% of total receivables, compared with 3.5% as of September 30, 2025.

ocf.heading: Net Cash provided by Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $866 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with $1,593 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The year-over-year decrease primarily reflects lower net income, higher inventory levels, lower receivables generation, partially offset by lower trade payables and provision absorption.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text: We recorded revenues of $4,354 million and $12,983 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, relatively flat compared to the same periods prior year. In both the quarter and year-to-date periods, growth in Construction and favorable price realization in Agriculture were largely offset by lower Agricultural shipment volumes and lower Financial Services revenues.

Agriculture.text: Global agriculture market conditions remained challenging during the first nine months of 2026. Farm income and capital spending remained under pressure from elevated input costs, higher financing costs, and continued uncertainty related to trade and agricultural policy, resulting in subdued demand for agricultural equipment. While farmer sentiment remained cautious, commodity markets demonstrated signs of improvement, with pricing strengthening in certain crop markets. The Company continues to view the current environment as a cyclical market downturn and remains focused on disciplined production and inventory management, operational efficiency, strategic cost actions, and investment in Precision Technology and innovation.

Construction.text: Construction's net sales were $777 million and $2,217 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, an increase of 5.1% and 5.4% compared with the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. In the quarter, the increase was primarily driven by higher shipment volumes in North America, partially offset by lower volumes in South America. Year-to-date, the increase was primarily driven by higher shipment volumes in North America and a favorable market mix in EMEA, partially offset by lower volumes in South America.

Financial Services.text: The operations, key financial measures and financial analysis differ significantly for manufacturing and distribution businesses ("Industrial Activities") and financial businesses ("Financial Services"). Accordingly, management believes that certain supplemental disclosures are important to understanding our consolidated operations and financial results. For further information, see "Supplemental Information" within this section for supplemental consolidating data presented separately for Industrial Activities and Financial Services. Transactions between Industrial Activities and Financial Services have been eliminated to arrive at the consolidated data.
